title: Jelly caring for her sister; light complexions in the family
summary: Jelly looked after her sister and brother-in-law Victor Koloss; family skin color.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Oh, yeah, he got well, and I mean, he was able to take care of my sister and her husband, because he... my sister had an appendectomy, and her husband had lung removed, and he was taking care of that.
When did you... that was Victor Koloss. Yeah, Koloss. Is that what you pronounce the name? Yes, Koloss. He looked just like a Frenchman, too.
He looked like a white man. In fact, that's how my mother looked.
I was only in there home, and it was about a half an hour I had to visit. Well, my mother looked just like him.

My grandmother, too, looked just like him. That's why those kids all looked alike. In fact, my sister had so much light blood behind her, she didn't have a dark child. She's the only one that came out dark, and she blamed my mother for it, too. She never did forgive her for that, she said.
God made you one. I used to tell her all the time. I said, you don't believe in God if you think mother had anything to do with that. Yeah, that's right. Nobody knows.
